checks: No pack CSS leaks into Neander catalog chrome
Published screens use the same application blocks and styles installed for customers
Only model-declared navigation, modules, tabs, pages, and actions render

The initial full app uses the framework shell without an unrequested external header, count strip, search, or filter bar; collection controls remain inside their shared toolbar and customer CSS does not hide that toolbar
Entity inventories, directories, and registries use the shared collection and overlay record-detail flow rather than page-local table or split-view recreations
Closing record details restores the collection's full width; opening details overlays without resizing the table or causing page-level horizontal overflow
Dashboard metrics, sample badges, and overview chrome do not render unless requested by the customer
Controls and landmarks expose accessible names and keyboard behavior
Long and multiline content does not cause page overflow or clipped non-scrollable controls
Loading, empty, error, disabled, focus, and reduced-motion states use the shared framework
Tables collapse into mobile cards and intentional data scrollers remain reachable
No third-party logos or sample personal data ship in generated customer output

Workflow graphs support node and group dragging, explicit branch connections, reconnect/delete, pan/pinch/zoom, undo/redo, required inputs, scratch/templates, settings and host-confirmed save/publish/Live
Reports render host-provided aggregate values, retain failed preview requests, and expose contributing data
Structured notes open as a dedicated page, preserve failed saves, and confirm discard and deletion
Optional editors remain absent unless explicitly composed into the requested model
certification: Data Workspace Framework reference pilot; CRM is one optional scope and customer application data and business outcomes remain outside the pack
